newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU delay would be bad for Italy -- Fossa.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay would be bad for Italy -- Fossa.

text.p: Delaying the 1999 start date for Europe's planned monetary union would have very negative consequences for Italy, the chairman of the Italian employers' group warned on Sunday.

In an interview with German newspaper Welt am Sonntag, Giorgio Fossa, the head of Confindustria, spoke out against a delay, warning nations might revert to bad fiscal habits in the absence of the constraints imposed by the Maastricht Treaty.

"I am opposed to postponing the start date for the currency union because the fixed starting date has forced us to take steps to overhaul our economy. If there were a delay, what has been achieved in Italy could crumble," he said.

Talk of possibly delaying the start for currency union has grown louder in recent months as Germany and France, the nations seen to be essential to the success of a union, are experiencing extreme difficulty in meeting the strict entry goals.
Italy, which has made great efforts to squeeze its economy into shape for the start, however still suffers from a reputation of being less stability-oriented than other nations.

Some German policy makers have privately suggested that Italy might not yet be ready to join the currency union, particularly since it has been more relaxed about stability matters than, for example, the German Bundesbank.
While Fossa said Italy needed some time to work on its image, he also said there is no reason to exclude Italy from currency union.
"It makes no sense to withold membership from one of the world's most industrialised nations," Fossa said.
Fossa also said the discussion about Italy's participation may be slightly misguided. "Italy will not be the problem for Europe, there are many more serious problems."
